children: The Global Perspectives session, titled ‘The Intelligent Enterprise: Leadership in the Age of AI’, featured CP Gurnani, Influencer, Co-Founder and Vice Chairman, AIONOS, Former CEO & Managing Director, Tech Mahindra, in conversation with Parikshit Choudhury, Chief Business Officer for B2B and Customer Contact Group, MakeMyTrip

The 10th edition of the prestigious BW Hotelier Indian Hospitality Summit & Awards (IHA 2026), hosted at the JW Marriott New Delhi Aerocity, is bringing leading voices from across the hospitality industry for the next two days of conversations on the sector’s growth and evolution. With the theme ‘India’s Hospitality Decade: From Growth to Greatness’, the Summit will examine the opportunities, challenges and shifts shaping India’s hospitality landscape as the industry enters a defining decade.

The Global Perspectives session, titled ‘The Intelligent Enterprise: Leadership in the Age of AI’, brought together technology and business leadership perspectives to explore how artificial intelligence is reshaping enterprises, decision-making and the role of leaders in an increasingly AI-driven business environment.

The session featured CP Gurnani, Influencer, Co-Founder and Vice Chairman, AIONOS, Former CEO & Managing Director, Tech Mahindra, in conversation with Parikshit Choudhury, Chief Business Officer for B2B and Customer Contact Group, MakeMyTrip.

“If India has to meet the objectives of 2047, it has no other option but to meet tourism needs. The usage of technology has just scratched the surface, and we need technology to ease the consumer experience like DigiYatra,” said CP Gurnani. “If the focus is the customer, we should see what we can do a bit more better for them. We need to look at how technology can make the consumer experience simpler and more seamless,” Gurnani noted.

“If DigiYatra can store compliances, then why can't we do the same in hospitality? We have only used AI to the ground, and there is much more that technology can do for the hospitality industry,” he highlighted. “AI will take over every job but not hospitality. The hospitality industry is ultimately about people and the consumer experience, and technology should be used to make that experience better,” Gurnani said.

“AI gives you more opportunity to personalise and helps grow the business. With AI and generative data, it is easy to process a lot more information and use it to understand customers better,” said Parikshit Choudhury.“When you look at multiple ways of generating revenue, you have to think about consumer needs. The way consumers use a product changes, and businesses need to understand those changing needs,” he explained.

“When you talk about personalisation today, you try to be the unique person. There is a lot of data that is used to personalise, and AI gives you the opportunity to process that information at a much larger scale,” Choudhury said. “When a user transitions to becoming a leisure user, the use case changes and so do the nuances. Personalisation becomes important because the needs and behaviour of the consumer are different,” he added.

During this session, CP Gurnani also interacted with Kunal Vasudeva, Co-founder & MD, Indian School of Hospitality, discussing the role of technology, tourism and consumer-centric experiences in shaping the future of hospitality.

As the exchange drew to a close, the speakers made a strong case for cross-industry learning. By looking at how India's fastest-moving sectors are combining smart automation with creative leadership, hospitality executives were urged to build agile, tech-enabled organisations that keep guest trust and purpose right at the center.

The two-day BW Hotelier Indian Hospitality Summit & Awards (IHA 2026) encompasses over 25 sessions where hospitality veterans and experts across the nation gathered to provide diverse knowledge and insights. The Summit & Awards is a testament to BW Hotelier’s commitment towards revolutionising Indian hospitality by honouring the crème de la crème of the industry.
